flap.purpose: Every character on a flap tile; size derives from tile height (--fh = 1.45 x --fw).

key.purpose: Uppercase key labels and the pager.

tip-title.purpose: Airport name in the map tooltip, uppercase, sodium yellow.

body.purpose: The one-line status; 14px on phones; max 90ch.

column-label.purpose: Uppercase tracked headers above departure columns only.

shadows.name: caret-underline
shadows.purpose: The search caret on the current flap tile; not an elevation shadow.

motion.name: cell-flip
motion.purpose: One matrix cell flip, drawn as a hinge fold in the fragment shader.

motion.name: flap-step
motion.purpose: One drum card per DOM flap character; each half folds in 23ms.

motion.name: fold-bottom-ease
motion.purpose: New bottom half swinging down from 90deg.

motion.name: roll-cap
motion.purpose: Longest visible drum roll; longer distances skip ahead.

motion.name: char-stagger
motion.purpose: Delay between characters in a flap row.

motion.name: row-stagger
motion.purpose: Departure rows ripple down the board.

motion.name: time-true-ripple
motion.purpose: Destination cells flip with delay proportional to flight minutes; the longest lands at 1.7s.

motion.name: trace-revert
motion.purpose: A landed ambient trace's cell returns to its density card.

motion.name: key-ink
motion.purpose: Key ink colour change on hover and focus.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: Search caret; static under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Rolls, ripples and arcs swap instantly; ambient traces become a still sample at 35% alpha.

narrative.overview:
Everything on screen is part of one Solari split-flap board: a matte near-black housing that holds charcoal flap cards, warm-white printed ink, and a single sodium yellow for whatever is active right now. The world map is itself a matrix of square flap cells. A cell's brightness is its printed grey card, and there are six of them, never a gradient. Text appears letter by letter on flap tiles that roll through the drum to reach their character. Every change of state is a flip: cells, letters and rows. Nothing fades or slides.

Density is high and the chrome is low. The board fills the viewport edge to edge inside a single gutter. The only surfaces are the housing, the cards and a slightly lighter rail for transient notes, and depth comes from the card's own construction: lighter above the hinge, darker below, with a hairline of housing between the halves. The visual rejection the build carries out is the category default of a dark glowing globe with neon arcs and every route drawn at once. Route lines are thin, flat and yellow, and they appear only for the current scene or a handful of ambient traces.
keyCharacteristics: One housing, charcoal cards, warm-white ink, one sodium yellow.
Quantised grey density cards (six faces plus a dimmed face), like printed flaps.
Every state change is a flip with a hinge; letters roll through the drum.
Square map cells that move in whole cells when panned.
Condensed signage caps on tiles and keys; small tracked caps only for column labels.

rules.name: The One Sodium Rule
rules.body: Yellow is reserved for what is active, selected, focused or in flight. It is never used for decoration, headings or static emphasis; static emphasis is warm ink on label grey.

rules.name: The Printed Card Rule
rules.body: Map density uses the six quantised grey faces and nothing in between. Never interpolate a ramp or add a hue to density.

rules.name: The Drum Rule
rules.body: Flap text is uppercase and limited to the drum's character set (space, A–Z, 0–9, `. - : / ' & + →`). Accents are stripped, and anything off the drum becomes a hyphen. Tiles are fixed-width runs: text is padded or cut to the column length and never wraps.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed belongs to tiles, keys and the tooltip title. Running prose stays in Barlow at 13–15px.

rules.name: The Hinge Rule
rules.body: Any surface that looks like a card (flap tile, matrix cell, key, favicon) has a split: lighter above the centre, darker below, and a housing-coloured hairline at the hinge. A key draws this as a hard-stop gradient, not a soft one.

dos: Do build every new surface from the housing, flap cards and the rail; nothing else exists on this board.
Do reserve sodium yellow (#ffc629) for active, selected, focused or in-flight state.
Do show map density with the six quantised grey faces from the density palette.
Do make every state change a flip: a fold at the hinge for cells, a drum roll for letters, staggered row by row.
Do keep the map in square cells that move in whole cells.
Do swap state instantly under `prefers-reduced-motion` (no rolls, no ripple, static caret, still traces).
Do credit the route data source in the footer.
donts: Don't fade, slide or scale anything in or out; the board only flips.
Don't add soft gradients, glass, glows or elevation shadows. The only gradient allowed is the hard-stop hinge split of a card.
Don't round corners beyond 2px or use pills and circles; markers are square cells.
Don't draw the whole route network at once or add a glowing globe; arcs belong only to the current scene or the few ambient traces.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or tint the density cards.
Don't set prose in Barlow Condensed or on flap tiles; tiles carry short uppercase values only.
